chunks: Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

A man was brought before Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام who had stepped on a man's stomach until he defecated in his clothes. So he judged against him that his stomach be stepped on until he defecates, or else he must pay one-third of the blood-money.

key_terms.أَحْدَثَ فِي ثِيَابِهِ: defecated in his clothes as a result of the injury
key_terms.أَمِيرِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amir al-Mu'minin, Imam 'Ali عليه السلام in his capacity as ruler and judge
key_terms.ثُلُثَ ٱلدِّيَةِ: one-third of the prescribed blood-money compensation
key_terms.دَاسَ بَطْنَ رَجُلٍ: pressed or stepped on a man's stomach, causing bodily harm

ai.seo_question: What was the ruling of Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام for a man who pressed another man's stomach until he soiled his clothes?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a judicial ruling of Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام concerning bodily harm that caused severe humiliation and injury. It establishes retaliatory justice or financial compensation in a case of intentional physical abuse.
